text.en: Stands on Bilogora, the low range of hills in northern Croatia between the Drava valley and Bjelovar. It watches northern Croatia and the border with Hungary. A dual-polarisation radar replaced the older one at this existing site in 2022, as part of a six-radar national renewal.

Stands at Debeljak near Sukošan in the hinterland of Zadar, one of three new coastal sites. It covers northern Dalmatia, the Zadar archipelago and the Velebit coast. It went into service in spring 2022 as the first of Croatia's new Adriatic radars.

Stands on Goli near Labin in eastern Istria, overlooking the Kvarner Gulf. It covers Istria, Rijeka and the Croatian Littoral. Installation began in May 2022; it was the second of three new dual-polarisation radars on the Croatian Adriatic.

Stands at Gradište near Županja in eastern Slavonia, on the flat plain between the Sava and the Danube. It watches eastern Croatia and the borders with Serbia and Bosnia. Installed at an existing site in November 2021, it was the first of Croatia's six new Vaisala radars.

Stands on the summit of Uljenje on the Pelješac peninsula in southern Dalmatia, looking over Dubrovnik, the Neretva delta and the southern islands. Its dome went up in October 2022 and it began public operation that November, giving Croatia full radar coverage including the sea for the first time.
